item.title: Ahi indigenous workers take up job opportunities in Australia
item.description: Five more Ahi indigenous people from Lae, including one woman, are preparing to leave for Australia this weekend under the Lae Labour Mobility Program. The workers are among 21 Papua New Guineans selected for jobs with a casino food company in New South Wales.
item.content:encoded:
Five more Ahi indigenous people from Lae, including one woman, are preparing to leave for Australia this weekend under the Lae Labour Mobility Program.

The workers are among 21 Papua New Guineans selected for jobs with a casino food company in New South Wales.

Before their departure, the workers completed their oath and declaration at the Lae City Authority.

The latest group adds to the growing number of Ahi people accessing overseas employment opportunities. Nine Ahi workers are already working in Australia, while five more, including one female worker, will travel this weekend.

Lae City Authority representative Margaret Gelam said the program is giving Ahi people an opportunity to gain new skills, support their families and return with experience that can benefit their community.

Team leader Kekeng Nicky Kawambara said the program is creating pathways for more Ahi people to enter the workforce and improve their livelihoods.

Ahi representative Elizabeth Sinemau said the workers’ success shows the importance of providing opportunities for Indigenous communities.

She encouraged the workers to remain committed, work hard and proudly represent the Ahi community, Lae and Papua New Guinea while overseas.

The Lae Labour Mobility Program continues to create employment pathways for Ahi families through overseas work, skills development and income opportunities.

item.title: Fly Zibo communities dig channels by hand as drought dries river
item.description: Communities in the newly created Fly Zibo local level government [LLG] area of Middle Fly district, Western, are facing a severe humanitarian crisis, forcing residents to manually dig water channels as a 10-week drought continues to dry up major waterways. All nine wards in Fly Zibo rely entirely on the Fly River and surrounding lagoons for drinking water, food and transport.
item.content:encoded:
Communities in the newly created Fly Zibo local level government [LLG] area of Middle Fly district, Western, are facing a severe humanitarian crisis, forcing residents to manually dig water channels as a 10-week drought continues to dry up major waterways.

All nine wards in Fly Zibo rely entirely on the Fly River and surrounding lagoons for drinking water, food and transport.

However, prolonged dry weather conditions have dropped water levels to critically low levels, closing vital river shortcuts to Obo and Kiunga and turning once-navigable lagoons into mud flats.

Locals say lives are at risk as people are forced to walk long distances to reach the main Fly River channel.

The cost of fuel in the area has surged to K12 per litre, while the movement of essential food and goods has completely stopped.

Island schools across the LLG have been forced to close, although teachers remain in the communities awaiting further direction from provincial education authorities.

“The river that feeds us is dying. We are digging just to find water,” one community member said.

Fly Zibo LLG is currently among the most vulnerable areas in the province, prompting urgent calls for drought mitigation support from both the Western provincial government and the National Government.

Middle Fly acting disaster coordinator Jeremiah James told NBC News that relief supplies would be dispatched immediately, with formal impact assessments to be conducted during distribution.

“The plan from the Disaster Office is that we will not go and do assessments first. We are planning immediate relief supply needs,” James said.

item.title: Toroama reiterates Bougainville’s stand on independence

item.content:encoded:
Autonomous Bougainville Government [ABG] President Ishmael Toroama has reiterated that Bougainville’s push for self-governance is non-negotiable and cannot be diluted by administrative processes or performance benchmarks.

Speaking during the Joint Supervisory Body [JSB] meeting in Port Moresby on Wednesday, Toroama urged Prime Minister James Marape and the National Government to respect the 97.7 per cent vote for independence delivered in the 2019 Bougainville Referendum.

While acknowledging that Section 342 of the National Constitution gives the National Parliament the mandate to make the final decision, Toroama said the decision cannot be separated from the democratic mandate of the referendum.

He criticized the National Government’s formal position paper regarding a potential “non-affirming decision” by Parliament, stating that it is a masterpiece of bureaucratic evasion and historical revisionism.

He rejected suggestions that a parliamentary rejection would reset Bougainville back to an extended autonomy framework focused on drawing down powers and achieving fiscal self-reliance.

“Bougainville is moving away from the autonomy space, and let me make that clear,” Toroama said.

“The National Government is threatening our constitutional right to self-determination as if I were in a progress review or some corporate evaluation subject to an external yardstick that shifts political tides in the National Parliament.

“We do not need a clear pathway to revisit that question. The question has been asked, answered, and sealed in ink and blood.”

The President also raised concerns over decisions introduced in Parliament regarding a three-quarters voting threshold and specific timeframes, stating that these were made without joint consultation required under the Melanesian Agreement and the JSB resolution of Dec 5, 2025.

“Bougainville had no part in these decisions. As required by law, these were unilateral decisions made by the National Government and the Speaker of the National Parliament that affect our mandate,” he said.

He reminded leaders that the 2019 referendum was strictly supervised by the United Nations and certified by the current Speaker of Parliament, Job Pomat, during his tenure as Acting Governor-General.

He added that no objections or legal challenges were raised during the statutory 40-day appeal period following the certification.

Toroama confirmed that Bougainville’s stance is backed by the ABG House of Representatives, national MPs from Bougainville, and key regional accords including the Panguna Communiqué and the Buka Resolution.

He called on National MPs to fully embrace the Joint Consultation Report and the Melanesian Framework as the official roadmap forward, emphasizing that the UN and global partners continue to monitor the process.

“In the eyes of my people, there is legal justice and there is moral justice. With due respect, Prime Minister, Bougainville demands both,” Toroama concluded.

item.title: IPA launches awareness campaign in Milne Bay over new associations law
item.description: The Investment Promotion Authority [IPA] has deployed a awareness team to Alotau in Milne Bay Province to educate local executives on the newly enacted Associations Incorporation Act 2023, which supersedes the previous 1966 legislation. Official records show that of the 162 incorporated associations registered with the IPA in Milne Bay, only one group has successfully completed re-registration und
item.content:encoded:
The Investment Promotion Authority [IPA] has deployed a awareness team to Alotau in Milne Bay Province to educate local executives on the newly enacted Associations Incorporation Act 2023, which supersedes the previous 1966 legislation.

Official records show that of the 162 incorporated associations registered with the IPA in Milne Bay, only one group has successfully completed re-registration under the new legal framework.

The remaining 161 bodies are currently classified as unregistered and risk losing their legal status if they do not update their records.

IPA Company Examiner Andy Pomat said that failure to comply with the updated laws could disrupt operations for community and civil society groups across the province.

"All associations across Papua New Guinea have been removed from the central registry for re-registration. According to our records for Milne Bay, out of 162 associations, only one has re-registered," Pomat said.

"If you don't comply, we will strike off the association. Non-compliant groups will face financial penalties, which was not the case under the old act."

He said team members were assisting executives on the ground in Alotau to complete their documentation.

Re-registration is free during a one-year grace period. Groups that fail to re-register before the grace period expires on June 30, 2027, will be subject to penalty fees.

Executives seeking to register new associations can access the IPA digital portal at www.ipa.gov.pg.

Milne Bay marks the third province visited in the national outreach campaign, with the awareness team scheduled to travel to Maprik in East Sepik province next.

item.title: UPNG open campus to be established in Ambunti
item.description: Locals in the upper Sepik region will soon have access to University of Papua New Guinea Open Campus to furthering tertiary education and securing better employment opportunities. This plan was revealed by Ambunti local level government president Edward Wiruk during the opening of the 18th crocodile & arts festival in Ambunti Station.
item.content:encoded:
Locals in the upper Sepik region will soon have access to University of Papua New Guinea Open Campus to furthering tertiary education and securing better employment opportunities.

This plan was revealed by Ambunti local level government president Edward Wiruk during the opening of the 18th crocodile & arts festival in Ambunti Station.

He is working closely with director of UPNG Learning Center in Yangoru-Saussia, Maino Koloa, to bring this establishment into Ambunti.

This proposed learning center once completed will significantly reduce expenses, while creating more opportunities for tertiary education to locals in Ambunti and beyond.

It will also be the 4th Open Campus in East Sepik to provide matriculation, diploma, and degree programs of the University of Papua New Guinea in the province.

Wiruk highlighted that this will equip young people of Ambunti for employment opportunities from the proposed Frieda Mine. The proposed UPNG Ambunti Learning Center is expected to open next year.

item.title: Western Highlands backs lifeline aviation as Rapa commits K200,000 to MAF
item.description: The Western Highlands Provincial Government [WHPG] has pledged K200,000 to the Mission Aviation Fellowship [MAF] PNG, recognising the organisation's 75 years of delivering life-saving services to some of Papua New Guinea's most isolated communities. The funding commitment was announced during the launch of a new partnership between the Australian Government and MAF PNG at Kagamuga Airport in Mt Ha
item.content:encoded:
The Western Highlands Provincial Government [WHPG] has pledged K200,000 to the Mission Aviation Fellowship [MAF] PNG, recognising the organisation's 75 years of delivering life-saving services to some of Papua New Guinea's most isolated communities.

The funding commitment was announced during the launch of a new partnership between the Australian Government and MAF PNG at Kagamuga Airport in Mt Hagen recently, aimed at ensuring the continuation of essential aviation services that connect remote communities to healthcare, education, emergency response and other vital services.

The partnership will help MAF sustain its operations and expand its reach to communities that depend on air transport as their only reliable link to the outside world.

Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa praised MAF's decades of dedicated service to the Highlands and the nation, saying the provincial government's contribution is a token of appreciation for an organisation that has saved countless lives.

"For 75 years, Mission Aviation Fellowship [MAF] has been a lifeline for our people, reaching places where no roads exist and where aircraft are often the only means of transport," Rapa said.

"On behalf of the people of Western Highlands, I am proud to commit K200,000 to MAF in appreciation of its unwavering service to our province and Papua New Guinea. This is our way of saying thank you for standing with our people through medical emergencies, education, disaster response and community development."

He also called on other provincial governments, churches and development partners to continue supporting MAF's mission, saying aviation remains critical to delivering services to Papua New Guinea's remote communities.

Australian High Commissioner to Papua New Guinea Ewen McDonald said Australia's partnership with MAF reflects its commitment to ensuring every Papua New Guinean has access to essential services regardless of where they live.

"For those in remote communities, MAF's planes can mean the difference between life and death," McDonald said.

"They help patients reach health care, deliver essential supplies and connect communities when no other transport options exist. Australia is proud to support MAF as it continues serving Papua New Guinea."

MAF PNG Country Director Dom Sant said for the past 75 years the organisation has demonstrated how aviation transforms lives by transporting patients, medical supplies, construction materials and emergency relief to communities cut off by rugged terrain.

"Whether it is transporting a patient for urgent medical treatment, moving construction materials or responding to an emergency, our aircraft provide a vital connection. Australia's support will help us continue this important work," Sant said.

item.title: PNG must prepare early as El Niño risks increase
item.description: Papua New Guinea must strengthen public awareness and prepare early as El Niño conditions continue affecting parts of the country, an official says. President of Farmers and Settlers Association, Wilson Thompson, said changing weather patterns were already being observed, with some areas receiving less rainfall while others experienced only light drizzle.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea must strengthen public awareness and prepare early as El Niño conditions continue affecting parts of the country, an official says.

President of Farmers and Settlers Association, Wilson Thompson, said changing weather patterns were already being observed, with some areas receiving less rainfall while others experienced only light drizzle.

He said communities needed clear information to prepare for possible dry conditions in the coming months.

“Preparation must begin now,” Thompson said.

He said reports from parts of the country, including Eastern Highlands, showed some rivers and streams were recording lower water levels, while some water sources were beginning to dry up.

Thompson said the prolonged dry weather could affect food production, reduce crop yields and create serious challenges for families who depend on agriculture.

He said limited access to clean water could also increase health risks, including the spread of water-borne diseases such as typhoid and dysentery.

“Public awareness is important. People need to understand how to conserve water, protect food gardens and prevent diseases during dry periods,” he said.

Thompson called on government agencies and provincial administrations to strengthen drought preparedness programs and ensure communities receive timely information.

He said the impact of El Niño could go beyond agriculture, affecting water supplies, household incomes, electricity generation and essential services.

Schools could also face difficulties if access to safe drinking water becomes limited, while farmers should take steps to protect crops, livestock and water sources.

Thompson said stronger coordination between national and provincial authorities was needed to ensure response plans were ready before conditions became worse.

He said lessons from previous droughts, including food security initiatives supported by the National Agricultural Research Institute and other organisations, should guide current preparations.

“We cannot afford to wait. Early preparation and awareness are the best ways to reduce the impact of El Niño on our communities and economy,” Thompson said.

item.title: Hawa CS gets K3m expansion funding
item.description: The Hela Provincial Government has released K3 million to continue construction work at the Hawa Correctional Service facility, the second tranche of funding for the project. Governor Philip Undialu confirmed the release on Wednesday, stating that a total of K10 million has been committed for the development of Hawa CS, which will become the second Highlands Regional Correctional Centre.
item.content:encoded:
The Hela Provincial Government has released K3 million to continue construction work at the Hawa Correctional Service facility, the second tranche of funding for the project.

Governor Philip Undialu confirmed the release on Wednesday, stating that a total of K10 million has been committed for the development of Hawa CS, which will become the second Highlands Regional Correctional Centre.

"Hawa Correctional Service will have three new facilities that will increase capacity, enhance security, and focus on rehabilitation and skills development. The facilities are for high risk, juvenile, and female inmates. Upon completion, holding capacity will increase from current 50 inmates to between 200 - 300 inmates," he said.

Work is currently underway across all three new blocks.

The female wing is progressing with construction of the second storey while Juvenile block has completed first-floor brickwork and is now moving to the second level and the High Risk section has finished ground backfilling and is preparing beam structures and concrete works.

Governor Undialu said over the past three years, the provincial government, in partnership with the National Government, has invested more than K20 million into Hawa CS, with further funding to continue through ongoing activities.

The next phase of the project will shift focus to rehabilitation and reintegration programs.

"Plans are in place to construct a Technical Vocational Education Training and FODE centre at the correctional service. The goal is to ensure prisoners are not merely incarcerated, but are rehabilitated, trained, and equipped with practical skills to return to their communities as productive and responsible citizens," he said.

A proper church facility will also be built within the institution to provide moral guidance, counseling, and spiritual rehabilitation.

The completed facility will feature modern security systems including CCTV surveillance, alarm systems, magnetic doors, secure watchtowers, and separate accommodation for convicted prisoners and remandees.

item.title: ‘Drowning in Waste’: Port Moresby’s flooded streets and the Coral Triangle crisis
item.description: In Papua New Guinea’s capital, rising floodwaters are carrying more than rain, they carry the weight of waste, mismanagement, and neglect.
